nodes.label: Applied migrations are immutable
nodes.rationale: Editing an already-applied sql/NNN file (even a comment) blocks db:migrate on a running deployment while staying green on an empty CI database; corrections must ship as a new migration.

nodes.label: RLS ENABLE without FORCE is inert

nodes.label: 4xx returned inside withTenant commits

nodes.label: Keyset cursor microsecond precision trap
nodes.rationale: timestamptz microseconds vs JS Date milliseconds silently skip rows; carry created_at as full-precision text instead of re-parsing to Date.

nodes.label: Frozen OpenAPI snapshot / INTENTIONALLY_EVOLVED_PATHS
nodes.rationale: The snapshot test is add-only subset; evolution goes through an allow-list rather than editing the snapshot, so silent contract regressions cannot be normalised.

nodes.label: Varnish edge cache auto-activation (ADR-0042)

Staging activation exposed three bugs that reported success while not working (space in ban expression, Bun sending BAN as GET, sql/068 RLS policy using the wrong GUC).

nodes.label: ADR-0002 Bun-only runtime & tooling
nodes.rationale: Two runtimes add behavioral branching, toolchain size, and bug surface; Bun provides runtime, package manager, test runner, and built-in APIs sufficient for the base.

nodes.label: ADR-0003 PostgreSQL + RLS multi-tenant isolation
nodes.rationale: App-level tenant_id filtering alone is fragile; RLS FORCE + non-superuser role gives defense-in-depth so one forgotten filter cannot leak cross-tenant data.

nodes.label: SECURITY DEFINER bootstrap-read checklist (ADR-0003)
nodes.rationale: Pre-tenant-context lookups (hostname/tenantCode -> tenant_id) need SECURITY DEFINER functions; safety comes from correct owner (bootstrap NOLOGIN role) + static SQL + narrow columns + REVOKE from PUBLIC + locked search_path, verified empirically.

nodes.label: ADR-0004 RBAC + ABAC default-deny baseline
nodes.rationale: RBAC alone cannot express attribute-dependent rules (ownership, scope, self-approval); default-deny + deny-overrides-allow keeps access safe-by-default and auditable.

nodes.label: ADR-0005 Soft delete for master/config, immutability for posted data
nodes.rationale: Physical delete destroys audit trail and breaks references; posted/append-only events must not be retroactively edited, corrected via reversal/adjustment rows.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0005 soft delete for master/config, immutability for posted data

nodes.label: ADR-0006 Offline-first + transactional outbox + sync HMAC

nodes.label: ADR-0040: site_search module admission
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: Admits site_search as an Official Optional Module (type domain, isCore false, deps only tenant_admin + identity_access) because cross-content search is a generic need of every public site; PostgreSQL FTS is the default until proven insufficient, keeping the module offline-lan-safe. Adapted from awcms-micro ADR-0031; schema lands in sql/064, permissions in sql/065.

nodes.label: SearchSourceDescriptor (descriptor-list contribution seam)
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: Modelled as a descriptor-list on ModuleDescriptor.searchSources rather than a capability `provides`, because checkCapabilityBindings raises capability_provider_conflict when more than one module declares the same provides string — and MANY content modules are expected to contribute search sources. Descriptor is PURE DATA (no executable extractor crossing the seam): table/column names, declarative publication filter, weight, privacyClassification; the generic engine binds values as parameters and only interpolates strictly validated identifiers. MODULE_CONTRACT_VERSION 2.1.0 -> 2.2.0 (additive MINOR).

nodes.label: Inward contribution direction (DAG-safe aggregator)
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: Content modules are PROVIDERS, site_search is the CONSUMER/aggregator. The naive design (search imports every content module) would drag a dependency onto each new content module; inverting it — content DECLARES sources, search discovers them via listModules() — keeps site_search ignorant of any specific content module and the dependency graph acyclic. Invariant enforced by tests/site-search-module.test.ts: no module names site_search in dependencies or consumes.

nodes.label: awcms_site_search_documents index projection
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: Tenant-scoped FORCE-RLS table, one doc per (tenant, source_key, resource_id, locale), tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS STORED with setweight A/B/C/D + GIN; pg_trgm on title ONLY for typeahead suggestion. Deterministic idempotent reconcile/rebuild plus single-resource reindex defends against stale-leakage. Accepted cost: a second projection on top of per-module search_vector, needed because blog_content publishes lifecycle as a log line rather than a real outbox event.

nodes.label: ts_headline sentinel snippet escaping
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: ts_headline marks matches with a NON-HTML sentinel, the whole string is HTML-escaped, then sentinels are replaced by <mark> — so markup coming from indexed content can never survive to the browser.

nodes.label: :tenantCode URL template adaptation
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: awcms public content routes are PATH-tenant-scoped (/blog/:tenantCode/:slug, ADR-0009) rather than host-resolved like awcms-micro, so descriptors carry a :tenantCode placeholder resolved server-side once per run from awcms_tenants.tenant_code and URL-encoded. Storing the FINAL url (rather than prefixing at query time) means a tenant rename is picked up automatically by the next reconcile via source_checksum.

nodes.label: Search index is never an authorization source
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: Publication state is filtered at the source->index boundary; the index query is a projection of public content only and the content module remains the source of truth for visibility. Every query is bounded by tenant_id AND locale (RLS FORCE + explicit predicate), and buildSearchCacheKey refuses to build a key lacking tenant+locale+query-hash.
nodes.norm_label: search index is never an authorization source

nodes.label: ADR-0041: comments module admission
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: Admits comments as a moderation-first Official Optional Module over PUBLISHED resources. What distinguishes it from site_search: it is an UNAUTHENTICATED PUBLIC WRITE surface, so the design question shifts from ownership of an index to what keeps an anonymous write path from becoming a stored-XSS vector, an unpublished-content oracle, or a spam channel. Adapted from awcms-micro ADR-0032; sql/066 schema, sql/067 permissions.

nodes.label: commentableResources descriptor seam
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: Same shape and same reason as searchSources: many content modules will want comments, and a second provider would trip capability_provider_conflict. MODULE_CONTRACT_VERSION 2.2.0 -> 2.3.0. Pure data descriptor; identifiers are re-validated with assertSafeIdentifier/assertSafeTableName immediately before interpolation — the registry gate (comments:resources:check) and the second validation are deliberately redundant: the gate proves the committed registry is clean, the runtime check proves the string reaching tx.unsafe is clean however it got there.

nodes.label: Store plain text, escape on render (anti stored-XSS by construction)
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: Bodies are stored as raw plain text, never HTML; at render EVERY character is escaped first, then bare http(s) URLs are autolinked with href and visible text both escaped plus rel="nofollow ugc noopener noreferrer". No allow-list sanitizer that can be wrong, and no path by which a stored comment reaches a browser as markup.
nodes.norm_label: store plain text, escape on render (anti stored-xss by construction)

nodes.label: Uniform oracle-free public submit response
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: Unresolvable resource, disabled module, anti-abuse block and accepted-but-held all return the same {"status":"received"}; only an immediately-public comment reveals its id. Author-bound operations return 404 rather than 403 when the caller is not the author, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe blocked terms or unpublished content.

nodes.label: Fail-closed server-side anti-abuse
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: Honeypot, HMAC-signed submit-time floor, length/link caps, per-tenant blocked terms, duplicate fingerprint, per-IP rate limit — all fail-closed: with the time floor active a MISSING token counts as too_fast, so deleting the token is not a bypass. The timing-token secret is a per-process random key with a warning rather than a source constant (a constant in a public repo is a signature that is not a signature).

nodes.label: Zero new AccessAction (spam marked via reject)
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: All eight permissions reuse existing AccessAction literals. Spam uses `reject` (identical blast radius, distinguished by an audited reason code) because inventing a new action plants a latent-authz trap: an action never seeded to any role denies even the tenant owner while the code looks correct.
nodes.norm_label: zero new accessaction (spam marked via reject)

nodes.label: Comment author PII minimization
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: Author email is never stored raw — only sha256 plus a masked form; IP and user-agent only as tenant-salted hashes. Notification subscription addresses are AES-256-GCM encrypted with a separate key; without the key what remains is an unresolvable sentinel, not plaintext. Retention ANONYMIZES in place rather than deleting, and respects legal hold.

nodes.label: Reply notification via domain-event outbox (no email dependency)
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: Reply notifications are published as a same-commit domain event whose payload carries only an opaque id, never a recipient address; the email dispatcher resolves the encrypted address at send time OUTSIDE the DB transaction (ADR-0006). Consequence: comments has no dependency on email, and a deployment without an email provider still works fully for commenting.
nodes.norm_label: reply notification via domain-event outbox (no email dependency)

nodes.label: ADR-0042: Varnish edge-cache tier, off by default
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: awcms is online-first (ADR-0035) with unlimited tenant subdomains, so every anonymous reader of the same public page triggers identical database work. ETag/Last-Modified saves only bandwidth and src/lib/redis/ still wakes the app; what was missing is a layer that answers WITHOUT touching the application. Shipped as infrastructure in src/lib/edge-cache/ (not a module: no tenant table, no permission, no admin screen) and genuinely no-op when EDGE_CACHE_MODE is unset — adding a subsystem to every public request's hot path is only legitimate if 'off' is actually free.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0042: varnish edge-cache tier, off by default

nodes.label: decideCacheability fail-closed allow-list
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: A pure function that denies by default; a response is cacheable only after passing EVERY check (registered surface, GET/HEAD, no Authorization, no awcms_-prefixed cookie, safe status, no Set-Cookie, no private/no-store/no-cache, not Vary:*, tenant resolved, query params allow-listed). New routes are not cacheable until someone declares them — forgetting is safe. Identity cookies are matched by PREFIX rather than a name list so tomorrow's new identity cookie cannot quietly open a hole; a test reads ssr-session.ts to enforce the real cookie names still match.

nodes.label: Origin-pressure auto-activation (pressure changes HOW LONG, never WHAT)
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: Mode auto measures request rate + origin latency in a rolling window: relaxed origin advertises TTL 0 (live data, cold cache), past threshold TTL ramps to full at twice the threshold with hysteresis to avoid oscillation. Pressure is deliberately NOT an input to decideCacheability, making it structurally impossible for a load spike to turn a private response public.
nodes.norm_label: origin-pressure auto-activation (pressure changes how long, never what)

nodes.label: Layered defence against Varnish cache-by-default
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: A shared cache in front of a multi-tenant app is a cross-tenant leak engine by default — stock VCL caches any 200 without cache directives for default_ttl (120s). Three independent mechanisms must fail before an unlabelled response is cached: the app labels EVERY response (including /admin and /api) with either Surrogate-Control or Cache-Control: private, no-store (no silent third state); VCL is default-deny in vcl_backend_response; and varnishd runs with -p default_ttl=0. A deny-list ('cache everything except /admin') was rejected as exactly the failure mode that makes shared caches dangerous.

nodes.label: Anchored surrogate-key invalidation via durable purge queue
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: Responses carry Surrogate-Key (t:<tenant>, :m:<module>, :s:<surface>, :r:<type>:<id>) and invalidation is a ban() regex over that header. Keys are restricted to [A-Za-z0-9:._-] when built AND re-validated in VCL, because a `.*` key turns one invalidation into a single-request denial-of-service; matching is anchored with (^|[[:space:]])key([[:space:]]|$) so banning t:abc does not evict t:abcdef. The literal-space first version made Varnish's whitespace token split produce 'Wrong number of arguments' while the handler still answered 200 — invalidation never worked at all, discovered only with Varnish really in front of staging. Enqueue happens in the same content transaction (outbox pattern, ADR-0006); delivery is a leased, retrying worker.
nodes.norm_label: anchored surrogate-key invalidation via durable purge queue

nodes.label: Bounded cache key space via allowedQueryParams
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: The edge keys on the full URL including query string, so unbounded queries mean unbounded cache entries and anyone can evict hot objects with cheap repeated requests. Each surface declares allowedQueryParams; anything outside makes the request non-cacheable.
nodes.norm_label: bounded cache key space via allowedqueryparams

nodes.label: Host-resolved discovery surfaces deliberately not declared
nodes.author: @ahliweb
nodes.rationale: robots.txt/sitemap.xml/feed.xml/atom.xml/feed.json are the best cache candidates in the repo, but their tenant is set inside withSeoPublicTenant while serveDiscovery(request, ...) does not receive locals, so the route cannot publish edgeCacheTenantId. Declaring them anyway would produce a registry entry that reads as 'cached' while failing tenant resolution on every request — a dead declaration is worse than an honest omission.
nodes.norm_label: host-resolved discovery surfaces deliberately not declared

nodes.label: ADR-0043: src/lib boundary = technical infrastructure without a domain name
nodes.rationale: src/lib had become a second module system no gate watched: four namespaces (seo, theming, comments, search) carried a module's name and held that module's code, and seo_distribution's application layer referred UP into src/lib/seo along a path modules:dag:check cannot see because that validator reads the DECLARED graph, never an import statement. The cause was structural, not sloppiness — the module contract had nowhere to put presentation/delivery code. Issue #257; awcms-micro ADR-0038 decides the same question there.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0043: src/lib boundary = technical infrastructure without a domain name

nodes.label: src/modules/<module>/presentation/ layer
nodes.rationale: Route composition roots, middleware glue and browser client scripts get a named home inside the owning module. The layer is deliberately NOT enumerated in module-contract.ts — domain/application/infrastructure are not enumerated either; what is machine-enforced is the GATE, not the naming. An allow-list of composition roots inside src/lib was rejected: it documents the ambiguity then enforces the documentation, without removing the reason src/lib/<module-name>/ keeps reappearing.

nodes.label: modules:dag:check namespace/alias collision rule
nodes.rationale: The gate fails on a src/lib/<x>/ namespace colliding with a moduleKey exactly or via a registered domain alias (seo -> seo_distribution, search -> site_search, plus four more) — without aliases two of the four real cases would have passed. src/lib/logging/ is a RECORDED EXCEPTION rather than an exclusion (the DB-free logger primitive imported by ~139 files vs the logging MODULE which is the audit-trail service), so the test can prove it is DETECTED and merely excused.

nodes.label: tests/module-boundary.test.ts extended to src/pages
nodes.rationale: Routes are attributed to their owning module via api.routes (Issue #256) and every cross-module import must be declared by that owner. identity_access joins logging as foundational FOR ROUTES ONLY — the authorization chokepoint is reached from 184 route files and declaring it everywhere would tell a reader nothing while making it a dependency of nearly the whole registry. Making the boundary visible surfaced four hidden edges: three declared (theming->module_management, visitor_analytics->data_lifecycle, visitor_analytics->module_management) and one REMOVED (seo_distribution->visitor_analytics: extractReferrerDomain is a pure string->hostname function, moved to _shared). General rule: an edge that exists only because a pure helper sits in the wrong place should be deleted, not documented.

nodes.label: ADR index (Indonesian source)
nodes.rationale: Indonesian is the SOURCE of the bilingual pair (ADR-0023); the English README.md is generated from it and staleness-gated by an i18n-source-hash comment.

nodes.label: ADR index and lifecycle rules (English)
nodes.rationale: One decision = one NNNN-kebab-title.md; ADRs are NEVER deleted (replaced ones are marked Superseded by ADR-XXXX and referenced by the new one); valid statuses Proposed/Accepted/Deprecated/Superseded; changes to binding standards require an ADR. Records the amendment chain ADR-0001 -> ADR-0022 (ERP modules in extension repos) -> superseded by ADR-0034 (three direct-use family templates).

nodes.label: 14-sprint implementation blueprint
nodes.rationale: Target sprint plan (foundation -> finance -> inventory -> logging/pooling -> procurement -> sync -> manufacturing -> HR/payroll -> tax/Coretax -> external business integration -> UI/reporting/AI -> workflow/security/deploy) written when the repo had no src/ at all. Principles: build-first (every sprint keeps the repo buildable), skeleton-first, NO fake completion (skeletons carry explicit TODOs and are never claimed production-ready), security-first, soft-delete-first. Its .env block is preserved unedited as a record even though APP_TIMEZONE and AUTH_JWT_SECRET never materialized — the binding contract is .env.example enforced by validate-env.ts, where only APP_ENV, APP_URL and DATABASE_URL are required.

nodes.rationale: Skeleton Done requires module contract, response/error helper, tenant-context helper, audit helper, domain-event helper, migration runner, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI baseline, health endpoint, passing build and initial docs; Implementation Ready adds tenant/profile/auth, ABAC guard, RLS context, redaction, transaction wrapper, idempotency wrapper, API contract and test skeleton.

Uses a retail/POS domain as a running ILLUSTRATION — the patterns and standards are reusable, the entities and endpoints are examples; real domain modules live directly in src/modules/ per ADR-0034/0035.

nodes.label: Five module categories and admission criteria
nodes.rationale: Core / System / ERP Domain Module / Derived Application (vertical) / External Integration, mapped to ModuleType base|system|domain|integration|derived. Core must be offline-lan-safe, needs an ADR plus two maintainer approvals, and may never depend on System/Domain modules; System may wrap external providers only off-by-default; External Integration lives INSIDE the owning module rather than as a top-level registry entry. §8's target module map is explicitly marked STALE as of 2026-07-25 (the registry now has 21 live modules) while §3 and §4 remain binding.

nodes.label: Admission decision tree with Q5 runtime-code gate first
nodes.rationale: The 'does this involve runtime code upload/install/marketplace/eval from tenant or third-party input?' question is deliberately placed BEFORE the Core question rather than on a single branch, so every category passes through that gate with no shortcut.
nodes.norm_label: admission decision tree with q5 runtime-code gate first

nodes.label: Trusted static registry policy (no marketplace, no runtime install)
nodes.rationale: src/modules/index.ts is the ONLY registry, compiled into the same monolith binary and reviewed through normal PR/CODEOWNERS/CI — never loaded dynamically from tenant-supplied files/URLs/packages. awcms_tenant_modules stores only enable/disable booleans for code already in the running binary; flipping a row never fetches or executes new code. Marketplaces, tenant plugin/theme upload, dynamic import() from tenant input and eval/new Function of non-committed text are banned without exception — executing unverified code over financial data is unacceptable, and relaxing it would require a new ADR superseding ADR-0001.
nodes.norm_label: trusted static registry policy (no marketplace, no runtime install)

nodes.label: Lifecycle dependency vs capability dependency
nodes.rationale: Two independent graphs. ModuleDescriptor.dependencies entries are ALWAYS required (enable/disable ordering) — there is deliberately no 'optional lifecycle dependency': if a relationship can vanish without breaking function it is a capability dependency, not a lifecycle one. capabilities.consumes entries must explicitly state optional true/false, and the module README must document what degrades when the capability is unavailable.

nodes.label: offline-lan-safe vs full-online-only compatibility classes
nodes.rationale: Full-online provider behaviour is always explicit opt-in, never default; a full-online-only proposal must PROVE (with a regression test, not a narrative claim) that the offline-lan profile stays 100% functional with the flag false.

This is the inverse of the usual failure mode — not code without docs, but repo rules promising a foundation layer that was never built — and its practical consequence is that an agent reading docs/adr/ concludes organization_structure can be called. Reason: seven modules that consume one another's contracts will harden into the wrong shape if the boundaries are only set after three of them exist.

nodes.label: Unlimited-subdomain junction (Cloudflare DNS + host-resolved routes)
nodes.rationale: tenant_domain already exists (PR #219, sql/046-048) but three things are missing: the Cloudflare adapter is absent-safe and tested yet called by no route, host-resolved public routes are unwired (src/middleware.ts was deliberately untouched during the port), and automatic subdomain provisioning naturally belongs to tenant_provisioning as one idempotent resumable run. Recommended order: wire the adapter + host-resolved routes as their own PR FIRST, then let provisioning orchestrate it — reversing that means writing provisioning steps against an unproven seam. Once unlimited subdomains are live, the edge cache key MUST include Host (already enforced in vcl_hash).

nodes.label: Committed snapshot of Claude Code agent memory
nodes.rationale: Agent memory lives outside the repo (~/.claude/projects/<slug-cwd>/memory/), so it is not cloned and is lost when switching devices; this generated file is its committed snapshot. memory:docs:sync (memory->docs, run before every commit that touches memory), memory:docs:restore (docs->memory on a new device, OVERWRITES same-named files) and memory:docs:check. The active memory is the source of truth, not this document. Because the repo is public, content is sanitized (session ids dropped, home paths replaced, password-shaped placeholders redacted) and device-specific memories are deliberately excluded — leaving dangling wikilinks after restore, which is expected rather than corruption.
nodes.norm_label: committed snapshot of claude code agent memory

nodes.label: Generated API & event reference
nodes.rationale: Produced by api:docs:generate from the bundled OpenAPI + AsyncAPI and staleness-gated by api:docs:check inside bun run check — never edited by hand. Deliberately has no interactive version switcher and no external assets: it is generated 1:1 from the contracts committed at the same git tag, so reading a prior release means checking out that tag, and the file stays fully usable offline/LAN with any text editor.

nodes.label: Cross-cutting API conventions (auth schemes, tenant context, keyset pagination)
nodes.rationale: Three schemes: bearerAuth (opaque login token), tenantHeader (X-AWCMS-Tenant-ID) and syncHmac (HMAC-SHA256 over <timestamp>.<body> with node id and timestamp headers). Every operation states its security requirement explicitly — there is no implicit 'some endpoints just don't need auth'; api:spec:check's ALLOWED_PUBLIC_OPERATIONS allow-list keeps that reviewed. The tenant header is never the sole isolation boundary: RLS context comes from the authenticated session (defense in depth). Lists use opaque keyset cursors, never large offsets; oversized bodies get 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE in the same error envelope.

The gate also demands purge emission from EVERY module that owns a surface.

nodes.label: Three edge-cache bugs that only appeared when actually run
nodes.rationale: The layer passed review and bun run check and was still wrong in three places, all of which REPORTED SUCCESS while doing nothing: (1) literal spaces in the ban expression made Varnish's whitespace tokenizer reject every ban with 'Wrong number of arguments' while the handler answered 200; (2) Bun sends non-standard HTTP methods such as BAN as GET (both fetch and node:http, verified on 1.3.14 via varnishlog), so every purge fell through to origin and 404'd; (3) sql/068's purge-queue RLS policy used GUC awcms.tenant_id while withTenant sets app.current_tenant_id, making WITH CHECK NULL — which failed blog publish with a 500 once caching was enabled, fixed in sql/070. Common thread: sendEdgeCachePurge had no tests at all and a fetchImpl mock structurally cannot catch class (2) — it inspects arguments, not the wire. Acceptance test: warm to X-Cache HIT, purge, expect MISS then HIT; never trust exit codes.
nodes.norm_label: three edge-cache bugs that only appeared when actually run

nodes.label: Edge purge wire protocol and activation order
nodes.rationale: POST /__edge-cache-purge with X-Edge-Purge-Token + X-Edge-Purge-Key; VCL still accepts a real BAN method so operators can curl -X BAN, but the application cannot use it (Bun drops non-standard methods). Turn on the application side first, schedule the purge worker, then put Varnish in front. The container's EDGE_CACHE_PURGE_TOKEN must match the application's exactly — a mismatch silently 403s every purge while the site looks healthy, which is why security:readiness reports an endpoint-without-token as CRITICAL.
nodes.norm_label: edge purge wire protocol and activation order

nodes.label: Two deployed environments (production and staging)
nodes.rationale: awcms.ahlikoding.com (production) and awcms-staging.ahlikoding.com (staging) run on the same Coolify-managed Docker host behind Traefik. ONE Coolify app per environment, not one app with two domains — sharing an app means sharing env vars, which is exactly how staging ends up writing to production data. Same owner identifier in all three phases but never the same password: awcms_identities is unique on (tenant_id, login_identifier), so one address is three separate accounts, and sessions are opaque tenant-scoped hashes that cannot cross databases. A prior claim that three different AUTH_JWT_SECRETs separated sessions was corrected — that variable does not exist in awcms and there is no JWT in the session path.

nodes.label: Permission seed migrations do not reach pre-existing tenants
nodes.rationale: Permission seed migrations only apply to tenants created AFTER them, so landing a new module silently leaves existing owners without its permissions — symptom is 403 ACCESS_DENIED on a module that is 'already installed'. Happened in production on 2026-07-26 (the owner lost 18 permissions for comments/site_search/form_drafts after migrations 062-070). Backfilling awcms_role_permissions is a deployment STEP, and 'full access' must then be verified against ABAC deny policies, SoD rules and business-scope assignments — all three were 0 across environments, so RBAC really was the sole determinant.
nodes.norm_label: permission seed migrations do not reach pre-existing tenants

nodes.label: Development brought to line-by-line parity with production
nodes.rationale: Before 2026-07-26 dev was not a small production but a silently different environment: schema stopped at migration 30 (production 70), zero tenants, no .env, and the only LOGIN role was a SUPERUSER — so the most expensive bug classes (RLS leaks and permission 403s) were precisely the ones impossible to reproduce there. Now migrations/tables/permissions/RLS counts and the runtime role match; only AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE, TRUSTED_PROXY_ENABLED and EDGE_CACHE_MODE differ, each with a stated reason.
nodes.norm_label: development brought to line-by-line parity with production

nodes.rationale: Structural template rather than a real generated artifact: its banner concedes the body is STALE (it still says 'no modules' and 'no migrations' while the repo has 21 modules and 75 migrations) and points to ARCHITECTURE.md as the source of truth until repo-inventory-generate.ts is ported. Deliberately carries NO generation timestamp — a wall-clock stamp would make every regeneration diff — so it always describes the state at the commit it was committed at. Also records the reviewed RLS-exempt allow-list candidates (schema_migrations, tenants, permissions, modules) and the rule that no ERP business table may ever join it.

nodes.label: Varnish 7.5 edge-cache service
nodes.rationale: Not a standalone stack — an overlay in front of an already-running app service; Varnish does not terminate TLS, so a terminator must sit in front of it.

nodes.label: Adoption is a two-sided change
nodes.rationale: Starting the container alone adds a hop for no gain: the app must set EDGE_CACHE_MODE, purge endpoint and token and schedule edge-cache:purge. Enable the app side first, confirm Surrogate-Control, then put the container in front — that ordering avoids a stale-content window.

nodes.label: default_ttl=0 / default_grace=0 belt-and-braces
nodes.rationale: Even if vcl_backend_response were bypassed an untagged response gets zero TTL rather than Varnish's stock 120s, so three independent layers must fail before an untagged response is cached.

nodes.label: EDGE_CACHE_PURGE_TOKEN shared secret
nodes.rationale: A mismatch makes every invalidation fail with 403 and the site silently serves stale content — which is why security:readiness treats a configured endpoint without a token as a hard failure, not a warning.

nodes.label: Malloc storage sizing vs ban lurker
nodes.rationale: Bans are evaluated against every object until the lurker collects them, so an oversized cache makes invalidation slower, not merely memory-hungrier; size to hot content, not the total corpus.
nodes.norm_label: malloc storage sizing vs ban lurker

nodes.label: Bundled published OpenAPI contract
nodes.rationale: Generated artifact produced by bun run openapi:bundle from the root fragment plus openapi/modules/*.openapi.yaml; direct edits are silently overwritten and never reviewed as the source of truth.

nodes.label: Root OpenAPI source fragment
nodes.rationale: Holds only what every module shares (info/servers/tags/security plus schemas genuinely used by 2+ modules); it has no paths and is deliberately not independently valid OpenAPI.

nodes.label: 128 KiB application-level body size cap
nodes.rationale: Enforced independently of any reverse-proxy limit and rejected with the same error envelope as everything else, so the contract does not depend on deployment topology.

nodes.label: Data Lifecycle module (API surface)
nodes.rationale: HTTP surface deliberately excludes real archive/purge execution (an internal scheduled job); exposes only registry read, legal-hold create/release, read-only dry-run, and run history.

nodes.label: DataLifecycleDescriptor (HighVolumeTableDescriptor)
nodes.rationale: Trusted code-declared metadata from src/modules/_shared/module-contract.ts, never tenant/request-controlled.

nodes.label: DataLifecycleLegalHold
nodes.rationale: A hold overrides ordinary retention/purge and is checked first, unconditionally; create and release are distinct default-deny permissions (maker/checker).

nodes.label: Domain event outbox + dead-letter replay
nodes.rationale: Consumers deliver redacted payload projections; dead_letter is the DLQ view; replay is permission-gated, reason-required, idempotent, audited.

nodes.label: Email module (API surface)
nodes.rationale: Two-tier ABAC (notification.create for all, announcement.create for role/tenant targets); truncated response means partial send that must be re-targeted.

nodes.label: Foundation module (health/pool probes)
nodes.rationale: Unauthenticated liveness and DB pool/work-class/circuit-breaker health that never exposes tenant data.

nodes.label: AuditEvent
nodes.rationale: Tenant-scoped audit trail row (actor, moduleKey, action, resource, severity, correlationId) written by recordAuditEvent across every module.

nodes.label: Media Library module (API surface)
nodes.rationale: ADR-0036 ownership inversion: owns the tenant media registry presigned-upload/finalize/cancel surface (moved out of news-portal) plus the managed-media enforcement switch; keeps the News Media tag deliberately.

nodes.label: NewsMediaObjectItem (media registry object)
nodes.rationale: Object lifecycle pending_upload -> uploaded -> verified -> attached; finalize does a real R2 GET + magic-byte MIME sniff + server-side SHA-256, never a bare HEAD.

nodes.label: Managed-media enforcement (one-way switch, ADR-0036)
nodes.rationale: Enabling forces content media references to resolve to verified same-tenant registry objects; deliberately one-way with no disable counterpart because self-disabling media validation is a confirmed exploit this design prevents.

nodes.label: News Portal module (API surface)
nodes.rationale: Admin surface for homepage sections and ad placements; every referenced media object must be a verified/attached R2 media object for the tenant.

nodes.label: Profile Identity module (API surface)
nodes.rationale: Person/organization profiles with typed masked identifiers, cross-module entity links, and identifier-based resolution.

nodes.label: Reporting module (management reporting + projections)
nodes.rationale: Reads-across summaries (access-audit, email-health, sync-health, module-usage, tenant-activity) plus idempotent projection rebuild/reconcile and checksum-verified export download.

nodes.label: SEO & Distribution module (API surface)
nodes.rationale: Tenant SEO config, redirect governance, and privacy-minimized 404 telemetry; public discovery routes (robots/sitemap/feeds) are Astro routes, not part of this REST contract.

nodes.label: Frozen open-redirect guard
nodes.rationale: Redirect targets must be a relative same-origin path or an absolute URL to one of the tenant's verified hosts; unsafe/cross-host/protocol-relative/CRLF/loop/over-long-chain targets rejected.

nodes.label: Sync Storage module (API surface)
nodes.rationale: Admin bearer-session views (conflicts/nodes/object-queue) distinct from the machine-to-machine HMAC push/pull/status/objects endpoints.

nodes.label: HMAC-authenticated sync (push/pull/status/objects)
nodes.rationale: syncHmac + tenantHeader security with SyncNodeId/Timestamp/Signature; push is idempotent per batchId, pull is checkpoint-based; a deactivated node is rejected 403 immediately.

nodes.label: Tenant Admin module (offices/settings/setup)
nodes.rationale: Offices CRUD with soft-delete/restore, tenant settings, and the one-time setup/initialize bootstrap that self-locks.

nodes.label: Tenant Domain module (hostname mappings)
nodes.rationale: Manual-first domain verification and single-primary selection; duplicate hostname always returns a generic conflict that never reveals cross-tenant ownership.

nodes.label: Theming module (draft/publish/rollback)
nodes.rationale: Data-only theme config validated against a build-time theme descriptor (CSS-injection spine); publish creates immutable versions; token values validated against strict CSS grammars.

nodes.label: Visitor Analytics module (API surface)
nodes.rationale: Public anonymous fire-and-forget beacon (always 202, never leaks tenant existence) plus permission-gated dashboards; raw detail hidden unless the caller holds raw_detail.read.

nodes.label: Workflow Approval module (API surface)
nodes.rationale: Versioned workflow definitions (draft/active/retired), a consolidated approval inbox, quorum-gated task decisions, delegations, and administrative force/reassign recovery; self-approval denied.

nodes.label: Negative-claim decay: absence claims rot silently unlike positive claims
nodes.norm_label: negative-claim decay: absence claims rot silently unlike positive claims

nodes.label: src/lib boundary: technical infrastructure only (ADR-0043)
nodes.rationale: src/lib had grown into a second, ungated module system: four namespaces carried module names and seo_distribution reached UP into src/lib/seo through a path the DAG validator could not see. The cause was structural — the module contract had nowhere for presentation code — so presentation now lives in src/modules/<m>/presentation/.

nodes.label: modules:dag:check namespace-collision gate
nodes.rationale: Fails when a src/lib/<x>/ namespace collides with a moduleKey exactly or via a registered domain alias (seo->seo_distribution, search->site_search); without aliases two of the four real cases would pass.

nodes.label: logging/ documented namespace exception
nodes.rationale: A database-free logger primitive used by ~139 files including src/lib itself; the logging MODULE is an audit-trail service that merely shares the word. A test proves logging is DETECTED and only silenced by the exception table, so the exception is not a detection blind spot.

nodes.label: client.ts pool kinds app/worker/setup
nodes.rationale: WORKER_DATABASE_URL/SETUP_DATABASE_URL are opt-in and fall back to DATABASE_URL, so separate kinds still give pool isolation even before role separation is adopted.

nodes.label: withTenant work-class + circuit-breaker gate
nodes.rationale: Applied in front of the pool before RLS SET LOCAL, so every route already using withTenant is protected without editing route files; non-interactive load passes an explicit workClass.

nodes.label: awcms_app fail-closed default GUC
nodes.rationale: app.current_tenant_id defaults to the zero UUID, so a query without withTenant returns zero rows rather than erroring or leaking another tenant's data; only a non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS, non-owner role makes FORCE RLS a real boundary.

nodes.label: Blog Content module README
nodes.rationale: First domain module registered directly in the base; admin CRUD/lifecycle, append-only revisions, public /blog/{tenantCode} and /news routes, and content-quality checklist gating.

nodes.label: Author-own-draft ABAC ownership override
nodes.rationale: Business-logic ALLOW override layered on top of identity-access evaluateAccess (call it first, then fall back to ownership check only when the sole deny reason is default_deny) rather than a new cross-module primitive.

nodes.label: comments is an unauthenticated public WRITE surface
nodes.rationale: That single fact drives nearly every design decision: the standing question is what stops an anonymous stranger from storing markup, enumerating unpublished content, or flooding the queue.
nodes.norm_label: comments is an unauthenticated public write surface

nodes.label: commentableResources descriptor seam
nodes.rationale: comments depends on Core only and never imports a content module; content modules DECLARE commentable resources as pure data and comments finds them via listModules(). A descriptor list rather than a capability provides, because many content modules will want comments and a second provider would trip capability_provider_conflict.

nodes.label: Publication boundary at resource->thread
nodes.rationale: A comment is only accepted against, or shown on, a resource satisfying its owning module's publicationFilter; the comment surface is never an authorization source for the resource underneath it.

nodes.label: Store plain text, escape then autolink
nodes.rationale: There is no sanitizer allow-list to get wrong and no path by which a stored comment reaches a browser as markup; only http(s) autolinks with rel=nofollow ugc noopener noreferrer are emitted.
nodes.norm_label: store plain text, escape then autolink

nodes.label: Uniform public responses (no oracle)
nodes.rationale: Unresolved resource, disabled module, anti-abuse block and accepted-but-pending all return {"status":"received"}; author-bound operations return 404 not 403 so they cannot confirm another author's comment exists.

nodes.label: Fail-closed server-side anti-abuse
nodes.rationale: Honeypot, HMAC-signed timing floor, length/link bounds, blocked terms, duplicate fingerprint and per-IP limits; with a timing floor configured a missing measurement counts as too fast, so stripping the token is not a bypass.

nodes.label: Minimized PII (hash, mask, AES-256-GCM)
nodes.rationale: With no subscriber key configured an unresolvable sentinel is stored rather than plaintext, so a missing secret degrades capability instead of leaking addresses.

nodes.label: comments:retention anonymization sweep
nodes.rationale: Anonymizes in place rather than deleting because the append-only moderation history must keep pointing at a row; skips tenants under an active legal hold.

nodes.label: comments:resources:check registry gate
nodes.rationale: Pure and database-free, and it runs BEFORE any SQL is built — which is the point, since the engine interpolates descriptor-declared identifiers.

nodes.label: Data Lifecycle module README
nodes.rationale: System Foundation module (ADR-0037): a module-contributed high-volume-table registry plus a safe lifecycle engine (dry-run, bounded archive/purge, legal holds) that never writes another module's table (ADR-0013 no-shared-table-write).

nodes.label: LegalHoldGuardPort cross-module enforcement
nodes.rationale: A delegated adopter's own purge function is the real enforcement point: it takes a LegalHoldGuardPort and skips its DELETE when the descriptor is held; the adapter is wired at composition roots to avoid a forbidden circular import (ADR-0011).

nodes.label: Opaque JSONB payload owned by the creating module
nodes.rationale: One table serves every multi-step form precisely because this module never learns domain knowledge it would then have to keep in sync with other modules.
nodes.norm_label: opaque jsonb payload owned by the creating module

nodes.label: Secret-shaped keys rejected, not redacted
nodes.rationale: A caller that gets a 200 cannot tell a stripped field from a saved one and would go on believing the secret round-tripped; the whole write fails with a 400 naming the offending path.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key on submit but not create
nodes.rationale: A retried create costs one deletable scratch row; a retried submit hands the payload to a domain action twice. Requiring a key everywhere trains callers to generate throwaway ones, weakening the guarantee where it matters.
nodes.norm_label: idempotency-key on submit but not create

nodes.label: No separate submit AccessAction
nodes.rationale: Submitting is a transition on a draft you may already edit, and an action nobody seeds into a role denies even the tenant owner while looking entirely correct in review.

nodes.label: Legal hold enforced at the purge, not in data_lifecycle
nodes.rationale: The data_lifecycle planner only READS this table, so a hold enforced inside that engine would stop nothing; the real gate is purgeExpiredFormDrafts asking LegalHoldGuardPort before DELETE. module.ts exports the lifecycle key and the purge imports it so the held key and the checked key cannot drift and fail open silently.
nodes.norm_label: legal hold enforced at the purge, not in data_lifecycle

nodes.label: MFA TOTP, recovery codes, session assurance & step-up (Issue #184)
nodes.norm_label: mfa totp, recovery codes, session assurance & step-up (issue #184)

nodes.norm_label: auth_notification port (email adapter, avoids cross-module insert)

nodes.label: Latent-authz trap: gate keys must match seeded endpoint keys
nodes.norm_label: latent-authz trap: gate keys must match seeded endpoint keys

nodes.label: Single-use enforced in DB (FOR UPDATE / CAS), not JS
nodes.norm_label: single-use enforced in db (for update / cas), not js

nodes.label: Descriptor sync from code registry to DB
nodes.rationale: Naturally idempotent, and refuses to write when the registry fails dependency-graph validation.
nodes.norm_label: descriptor sync from code registry to db

nodes.label: "Sync first" registry-row invariant
nodes.rationale: Registering a module in src/modules/index.ts does not create its registry row, and three tables FK to awcms_modules.module_key — so every tenant-scoped mutation calls syncModuleDescriptors itself rather than assuming an operator ran the sync endpoint.

nodes.label: Tenant module enable/disable lifecycle
nodes.rationale: A missing awcms_tenant_modules row means enabled-by-default (backward compatible); isCore modules cannot be disabled, preventing admin lockout; it writes a row and never unloads code.

nodes.label: Non-secret tenant module settings
nodes.rationale: Secret-shaped keys AND secret-shaped values are rejected at request time so they are never stored, reusing _shared/redaction.ts.

nodes.label: Navigation filtering is not authorization
nodes.rationale: Entries are filtered by module status, tenant enablement and required permission for presentation only; the endpoint guard remains the authority.

nodes.label: Registry-derived sidebar model
nodes.rationale: AdminLayout previously kept a hand-written array that had drifted into three entries pointing at non-existent pages and eight pages the registry had never heard of; a test now binds declarations to the filesystem in both directions.

nodes.label: Per-tenant sidebar arrangement stored as a delta
nodes.rationale: A snapshot would freeze each tenant's sidebar at the moment they first touched it; a delta lets a newly added module's nav entry appear everywhere with no data migration. Rows resolve BY KEY against the default and unmatched rows are ignored, so there is no path from a request body to a new menu link, and overrides apply BEFORE composition so they cannot carry an entry past requiredPermission.
nodes.norm_label: per-tenant sidebar arrangement stored as a delta

nodes.label: Tenant module presets
nodes.rationale: A preset enables what it lists and disables every enabled, unlisted, unprotected module — enable-only would make presets useless as a way to REACH a profile. Executed through the existing primitives one call per change so rejections are reported, not swallowed.

nodes.label: Reuse the stronger existing permission
nodes.rationale: An apply IS a sequence of enables and disables, so it guards on tenant_modules.disable; a new action would need a seed migration and an unseeded action denies even the owner.

nodes.label: Tenant-module matrix
nodes.rationale: Re-runs the REAL evaluate functions rather than a UI-side re-derivation that can drift; warnings are one-directional because asking evaluateModuleEnable about an already-enabled module short-circuits to an answer that looks like a check and is not one. No health column, since a per-row health read would be 21 reads in one transaction.

nodes.label: Module audit summary guarded by audit_trail.read
nodes.rationale: These are audit-log rows, so whoever may not read the audit log must not get a filtered view of it through another door; module_registry is excluded because descriptor sync's resource_id is not a module key.
nodes.norm_label: module audit summary guarded by audit_trail.read

nodes.label: Module-registry composition engine
nodes.rationale: Which modules exist is decided at build time, never from tenant input; the pure engine rejects duplicate keys, missing/cyclic dependencies, capability provider conflicts, profile incompatibility, navigation path conflicts and invalid jobs. It lives in the module rather than _shared so both reused validators import cleanly.

nodes.label: Health/readiness registry
nodes.rationale: Cheap bounded signals; GET is a passive read while POST .../health/check records history and runs any live provider check.

nodes.label: verification_status drift between JIT SSO and self-registration
nodes.norm_label: verification_status drift between jit sso and self-registration

nodes.label: SearchSourceDescriptor contribution seam
nodes.rationale: Pure data with a declarative publication filter — no executable extractor and no tenant SQL; only reviewed identifiers matching a strict pattern are interpolated into a parameterized query. Not modeled as a capability provides because more than one provider would trip capability_provider_conflict.

nodes.label: The index is a public-content projection, never an authorization source
nodes.rationale: Publication state is enforced at the source-to-index boundary so a draft, private, deleted or scheduled resource is never even read into it.
nodes.norm_label: the index is a public-content projection, never an authorization source

nodes.label: reconcile / rebuild / reindex indexing primitives
nodes.rationale: The scheduled reconcile is the deterministic backbone because blog_content publishes lifecycle as log lines rather than real outbox events; reindex is the low-latency primitive awaiting a real domain-event emitter.

nodes.label: Bound query parameter + validated identifiers
nodes.rationale: Query text is always a bound parameter into websearch_to_tsquery, and descriptor identifiers are validated before interpolation — the same discipline as data_lifecycle's generic execution mode.

nodes.label: ts_headline sentinel + escape then mark
nodes.rationale: Snippets use non-HTML sentinels which are escaped before becoming <mark>, so content-originated markup can never survive; index-time encodeURIComponent stops a source value injecting a path segment or scheme.

nodes.label: site_search port adaptations vs awcms-micro
nodes.rationale: Path-tenant URLs instead of host-resolved, no inline typeahead script because this base's CSP has no unsafe-inline, constant page labels because there is no i18n catalog runtime, and an added registry gate per this base's convention.

nodes.label: Host-based tenant routing seam
nodes.rationale: Additive to ADR-0009 path-based /blog/{tenantCode}; src/middleware.ts is untouched because host resolution is a per-public-route concern, leaving login/Turnstile/CSP guarantees unchanged.

nodes.label: SECURITY DEFINER host lookup function
nodes.rationale: Owned by a dedicated NOLOGIN/NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS role with a scoped FOR SELECT policy, EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC and granted only to awcms_app; reserved for the anonymous public resolver, never used by the authenticated management API.

nodes.label: resolvePublicTenantFromRequest resolution order
nodes.rationale: Only active domain plus active tenant resolves; every other case returns an identical null in exactly one round trip, so there is no timing side-channel. X-Forwarded-Host is read only when trustProxy is set.

nodes.label: Immutable hostname, atomic set-primary
nodes.rationale: is_primary is never settable through the generic PATCH and PATCH can never set status active; a duplicate hostname returns a generic 409 that never reveals whether it belongs to another tenant.

nodes.label: tenant-domain:dns:sync reconciliation job
nodes.rationale: A DNS write inside the tenant request would block on Cloudflare and a failure would leave a non-resolving row with nothing to retry it; an idempotent pass also heals a record edited by hand. The worker holds SELECT only, so a compromised worker cannot alter the hostname-to-tenant mapping.

nodes.label: Drifted records moved, never duplicated or deleted
nodes.rationale: Two A records for one hostname round-robin between old and new target, which reads as an intermittent outage; and nothing is deleted so a suspended domain leaves a visible harmless stale record rather than an automated destructive DNS write.
nodes.norm_label: drifted records moved, never duplicated or deleted

nodes.label: Dangling-DNS domain takeover residual risk (M1)
nodes.rationale: verify activates from in-row fields with no outbound ownership proof, and the global unique index is scoped WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, so a soft-deleted hostname is re-registerable — combined, tenant B can claim a hostname whose DNS still points at the platform. Custom-domain activation must stay operator-gated until real DNS-token proof is wired.
